carrier.description:
Name of the shipping carrier.

The carrier field identifies the logistics company responsible for delivering the shipment. Common carriers include DHL, FedEx, UPS, USPS, and regional carriers. This information is displayed to customers for tracking purposes.

**Format**: Free-form string with a maximum of 100 characters. Sellers should use the exact carrier name as provided by the carrier or a commonly recognized abbreviation.

trackingNumber.description:
Tracking number from the carrier for delivery tracking.

The tracking number is a unique identifier assigned by the shipping carrier to track the shipment's journey from origin to destination. Customers use this number to monitor delivery status through the carrier's tracking system.

**Format**: Free-form string with a maximum of 100 characters. The format varies by carrier (numeric, alphanumeric, barcodes). Sellers should enter the tracking number exactly as provided by the carrier.
trackingNumber.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to ecommerce_mall_shipments.tracking_number column. Non-nullable string storing the carrier-provided tracking identifier.

itemIds.description:
Array of order item IDs to include in this shipment.

The itemIds array specifies which paid order items are being shipped together in this shipment. All specified items must belong to the same order and seller, and must have "paid" status. Items already shipped, cancelled, or refunded cannot be included.

**Composition**: Each ID in this array creates a junction record in ecommerce_mall_shipment_items linking the order item to the created shipment.

**Constraints**: Minimum 1 item per shipment. All items must have "paid" status. All items must belong to the same seller. All items must belong to the same order.

Each order item ID in the array generates a shipment_item record linking the order item to the created shipment. All items must have "paid" status, belong to the same seller, and belong to the same order.

IEcommerceMallShipment.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new shipment.

Sellers use this DTO to create shipments bundling one or more paid order items with carrier and tracking information. All specified items transition from "paid" to "shipped" status upon shipment creation.

**Order Association**: The orderId is required when creating via /seller/shipments. When using /sellers/me/orders/items/{itemId}/ship, the order is derived from the path parameter.

**Item Requirements**: All order items must have "paid" status, belong to the authenticated seller, and belong to the same order. Items already shipped or belonging to another seller are rejected.

- ecommerce_mall_products: id, name, description, base_price, created_at, updated_at (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL)
- ecommerce_mall_categories: category details via JOIN on ecommerce_mall_category_id
- ecommerce_mall_sellers/ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles: seller profile via JOIN on ecommerce_mall_seller_id
- ecommerce_mall_product_images: images array ordered by display_order ASC
- ecommerce_mall_product_variants: variants array (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL), including optionValues via JOIN
- ecommerce_mall_reviews: AVG(rating) as averageRating, COUNT(*) as reviewCount

- Total orders represents all non-deleted orders
- Status-specific counts show order distribution across lifecycle stages
- Cancelled and refunded counts indicate customer service issues

- Monitoring platform order volume trends
- Identifying high cancellation rates requiring attention
- Tracking order flow through fulfillment pipeline

cancelledOrders.description: Number of orders with 'cancelled' status (all items cancelled).

Compute: COUNT(*) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL as totalOrders; GROUP BY status to get counts for paidOrders, shippedOrders, deliveredOrders, cancelledOrders, refundedOrders, partiallyCompletedOrders. Each status count filters orders WHERE status = '[status_value]' AND deleted_at IS NULL.

Order item volume and quantity statistics grouped by status.

Contains aggregated counts of all order line items across the platform, segmented by item-level status. These metrics provide granular insight into individual product fulfillment since each order may contain multiple items that can have different statuses.

Metrics breakdown:
- Total items represents all order line items
- Item-level status tracking provides more granular data than order-level
- Average quantity shows typical purchase quantities per item

Use cases:
- Product-level fulfillment analysis
- Identifying items stuck in specific statuses
- Understanding average order composition

orderItemStatistics.x-autobe-specification: Aggregated from ecommerce_mall_order_items table. Compute: COUNT(*) as totalItems; GROUP BY status to get counts for paidItems, shippedItems, deliveredItems, cancelledItems, refundedItems; AVG(quantity) as averageQuantityPerItem. Each status count filters items WHERE status = '[status_value]'.

Shipment creation and volume statistics.

Contains aggregated metrics about shipment activity across the platform, including total shipments created and average items per shipment. These metrics help administrators monitor shipping throughput and identify potential logistics bottlenecks.

Metrics breakdown:
- Total shipments counts all non-deleted shipments
- Total items shipped counts individual items across all shipments
- Average items per shipment indicates typical shipment size

Use cases:
- Monitoring shipping throughput
- Identifying oversized or undersized shipments
- Logistics capacity planning

Compute: COUNT(*) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL as totalShipments; COUNT(*) from ecommerce_mall_shipment_items as totalItemsShipped; totalItemsShipped / totalShipments as averageItemsPerShipment. Soft-deleted shipments excluded via WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.

fulfillmentPerformance.description:
Fulfillment performance indicators and rates.

Contains computed performance metrics that indicate how efficiently the platform fulfills orders. These key performance indicators help administrators monitor platform health and identify areas for improvement.

Metrics breakdown:
- Average fulfillment time measures speed from payment to shipment
- Delivery completion rate shows percentage of items successfully delivered or refunded
- Cancellation rate indicates the percentage of items that required cancellation

Use cases:
- Platform health monitoring
- Identifying fulfillment speed issues
- Tracking customer satisfaction indicators

- Business intelligence and reporting

IEcommerceMallOrder.IWarning.description:
Checkout validation warning representing a non-blocking concern discovered during cart validation.

Warnings inform customers about issues that may affect their order but do not prevent them from proceeding to payment. Examples include low stock quantities and price changes since items were added to the cart.

- LOW_STOCK: Available quantity is below the requested amount
- PRICE_CHANGED: Product or variant price has changed since the item was added to cart

Warnings are returned in the checkout validation response alongside errors. Unlike errors, warnings do not block checkout completion. Clients should display warnings to help customers make informed purchasing decisions.

All filter fields are optional and can be combined for precise filtering. Date filters use ISO 8601 format (date-time). The search parameter performs case-insensitive pattern matching on both seller email and shop name. Pagination defaults to page 1 with limit 20, maximum allowed limit is 100. Sorting defaults to created_at descending when not specified.
IEcommerceMallSeller.IAnalytic.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter aggregation for seller analytics. Filters and aggregates data from ecommerce_mall_sellers (approval_status, created_at, email), ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles (shop_name), ecommerce_mall_seller_suspensions (suspension state), ecommerce_mall_products (product_count), and ecommerce_mall_order_items (order statistics via JOIN through products).

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller.

UUID identifier assigned when the seller account is created. Used for all API references to this seller account.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_sellers.id. UUID primary key for seller identification.

email.description:
Seller's registered email address.

Email address used for account login and platform communication. Must be unique across all seller accounts.

oneOf.description: Current approval status of the seller account.
Current approval status of the seller account.
Current approval status of the seller account.

approvalStatus.description:
Current approval status of the seller account.

Indicates whether the seller registration has been reviewed by administrators. Pending sellers cannot list products. Rejected sellers may reregister with corrections.
approvalStatus.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_sellers.approval_status. Enum values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'. Indicates whether seller registration has been reviewed by administrators.

suspensionStatus.description:
Current suspension status. Null indicates no active suspension.

Indicates whether the seller account is currently suspended by an administrator. Suspended sellers cannot access the platform. Active status means the seller is in good standing.
suspensionStatus.x-autobe-specification: Computed from ecommerce_mall_seller_suspensions. Check for active record where ecommerce_mall_seller_id matches sellers.id AND restored_at IS NULL. Returns 'suspended' if active suspension exists, 'active' otherwise.

shopName.description:
Shop name from seller profile. Null if profile not yet created.

Public-facing shop name displayed to customers in product listings and seller pages. Set when the seller creates their shop profile.
shopName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles.name via ecommerce_mall_sellers.profile relation JOIN. Null if seller has not created a shop profile.

productCount.description:
Number of active products listed by this seller (excluding soft-deleted products).

Total count of products currently available for sale. Does not include products that have been soft-deleted by the seller.
productCount.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT of ecommerce_mall_products rows where ecommerce_mall_seller_id = sellers.id AND deleted_at IS NULL.

orderCount.description:
Number of orders containing this seller's products.

Total count of unique orders that include at least one product from this seller. Used for measuring seller engagement and order volume.
orderCount.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT of DISTINCT ecommerce_mall_order_items.ecommerce_mall_order_id where ecommerce_mall_order_items.ecommerce_mall_product_id IN (SELECT id FROM ecommerce_mall_products WHERE ecommerce_mall_seller_id = sellers.id).

totalItemsSold.description:
Total quantity of items sold across all order items for this seller.

Cumulative number of individual product units sold. Only counts items with 'shipped' or 'delivered' status, excluding cancelled or refunded items.
totalItemsSold.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM of ecommerce_mall_order_items.quantity for all order items where ecommerce_mall_order_items.ecommerce_mall_product_id IN (SELECT id FROM ecommerce_mall_products WHERE ecommerce_mall_seller_id = sellers.id) AND ecommerce_mall_order_items.status IN ('shipped', 'delivered').

totalRevenue.description:
Total revenue generated from all sold items (sum of quantity * unit_price).

Gross revenue in platform currency before platform fees. Calculated as sum of quantity multiplied by unit price for all shipped or delivered items.
totalRevenue.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM of ecommerce_mall_order_items.quantity * ecommerce_mall_order_items.unit_price for all order items where ecommerce_mall_order_items.ecommerce_mall_product_id IN (SELECT id FROM ecommerce_mall_products WHERE ecommerce_mall_seller_id = sellers.id) AND ecommerce_mall_order_items.status IN ('shipped', 'delivered').

createdAt.description:

Date and time in ISO 8601 format when the seller registered on the platform. Used for account age calculation and compliance tracking.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_sellers.created_at. Timestamp when seller account was created on the platform.

IEcommerceMallSeller.IAnalytic.ISummary.description:
Individual seller analytics record with aggregate metrics.

Contains seller summary information combined with computed performance metrics including product count, order statistics, and revenue totals for platform analytics and oversight.
IEcommerceMallSeller.IAnalytic.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Computed type combining ecommerce_mall_sellers, ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles, ecommerce_mall_products, and ecommerce_mall_order_items via JOINs. Aggregations: product_count, order_count, total_items_sold, total_revenue. suspensionStatus computed from ecommerce_mall_seller_suspensions active records.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order item.

This UUID uniquely identifies the order item within the system and is used for tracking, API references, and linking to related resources like cancellation requests, refund requests, and reviews.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.id. UUID primary key of the order item.

quantity.description:
Quantity of this product variant purchased in the order.

Represents how many units of this specific product variant were included in the order. The quantity is frozen at purchase time for accurate billing and fulfillment.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.quantity. Integer quantity of the product variant purchased.

unitPrice.description:
Unit price of the product variant at time of purchase, frozen at transaction time.

This price is locked in when the customer completes the purchase, ensuring accurate billing even if the seller later changes the product price. Multiply by quantity for line item subtotal.
unitPrice.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_order_items.unit_price. Float price per unit at time of purchase.

productName.description:
Product name frozen at purchase time from product snapshot.

This name is captured from the product snapshot created at order time, ensuring accurate display of what was actually purchased. If the seller later renames the product, this frozen name preserves the original order record.
productName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots.name via ecommerce_mall_order_items.productSnapshot relation. Frozen at purchase time for dispute resolution.

productImage.description:
Primary product image URL frozen at purchase time from product snapshot.

Displays the first product image that was active when the order was placed. This frozen image ensures the customer sees what they actually ordered, even if the seller later changes or removes product images.
productImage.x-autobe-specification: Computed from ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_images.url via nested productSnapshot.productSnapshotImages relation. Selects first image (display_order = 0). Frozen at purchase time.

IEcommerceMallShipment.IDelivery.ISummar.description:
Summary of a product item within a pending delivery.

Represents an individual order item that has been shipped by a seller and is awaiting customer confirmation. Product information is frozen at purchase time via product snapshots, ensuring accurate display even if the product is later modified.

**Frozen Product Data**:
The product name and image are captured from the product snapshot created at order time, preserving what the customer actually purchased.
IEcommerceMallShipment.IDelivery.ISummar.x-autobe-specification: Source: ecommerce_mall_order_items JOIN ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots ON product_snapshot_id. Fields: order_item.id, order_item.quantity, order_item.unit_price, product_snapshot.name (productName), product_snapshot.images[0].url (productImage). This is a joined query result combining order_items with product_snapshots and product_snapshot_images. All data is frozen at purchase time for dispute resolution.

IEcommerceMallProduct.IAnalytic.description:
Aggregated product analytics response containing computed statistics and paginated product list.

Statistics include total/active/deleted product counts, average/min/max base prices, category distribution showing product counts per category, and seller distribution showing product counts per seller. The paginated product list contains matching products sorted by creation date.

total_count.description:
Total count of all products matching the analytics filter criteria.

This count includes both active and deleted products. Use this to understand the complete scope of products in the dataset.
total_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT(*) aggregation of ecommerce_mall_products table. Represents total number of products matching the filter criteria (including both active and deleted products).

active_count.description:
Count of active products where deleted_at is null.

Active products are visible in listings and available for purchase. This is the primary metric for understanding currently available inventory.
active_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT(*) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL from ecommerce_mall_products table. Represents the number of currently active (non-deleted) products.

deleted_count.description:
Count of deleted products where deleted_at is not null.

Soft-deleted products are hidden from listings but retained in the database for order history and audit purposes.
deleted_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT(*) WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL from ecommerce_mall_products table. Represents the number of soft-deleted products.

average_price.description:
Average base price of all matching products.

This value is computed from the base_price field of products. Note that actual purchase prices may vary based on variant-specific pricing.
average_price.x-autobe-specification: AVG(base_price) aggregation from ecommerce_mall_products table. Computes the average base price across all matching products.

min_price.description:
Minimum base price among all matching products.

This represents the cheapest product in the dataset by base price. Variant-specific pricing may result in lower effective prices.
min_price.x-autobe-specification: MIN(base_price) aggregation from ecommerce_mall_products table. Returns the lowest base price among all matching products.

max_price.description:
Maximum base price among all matching products.

This represents the most expensive product in the dataset by base price. Premium products may have variant-specific pricing above this value.
max_price.x-autobe-specification: MAX(base_price) aggregation from ecommerce_mall_products table. Returns the highest base price among all matching products.

category_distribution.description:
Distribution of products grouped by category.

Each entry contains a category reference and the count of products assigned to that category. Use this to understand product distribution across the category taxonomy.
category_distribution.x-autobe-specification: GROUP BY category_id with COUNT(*) from ecommerce_mall_products table JOIN ecommerce_mall_categories. Returns array of ICategoryDistribution objects with category name and product count.

seller_distribution.description:
Distribution of products grouped by seller.

Each entry contains a seller summary and the count of products owned by that seller. Use this to understand which sellers have the most products on the platform.
seller_distribution.x-autobe-specification: GROUP BY seller_id with COUNT(*) from ecommerce_mall_products table JOIN ecommerce_mall_sellers. Returns array of ISellerDistribution objects with seller summary and product count.

items.description:
Paginated list of product summaries matching the analytics filter criteria.

Each item is a lightweight product summary containing id, name, basePrice, categoryName, hasStock indicator, seller summary, and timestamps. This is the same as IEcommerceMallProduct.ISummary used elsewhere.
items.x-autobe-specification: Paginated list of product summaries matching filter criteria, mapped as IEcommerceMallProduct.ISummary[]. Sorted by created_at DESC by default. Limited by pagination parameters.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the items array.

Contains page number, items per page, total count, total pages, and navigation flags to traverse through the paginated product list.
pagination.x-autobe-specification: Standard pagination metadata wrapping the items array. Follows IPage.IPagination schema with page, limit, total, totalPages, hasNext, hasPrev fields.

IEcommerceMallProduct.IAnalytic.x-autobe-specification: Aggregation type computed from ecommerce_mall_products table. Aggregations: COUNT(*) total_count, COUNT WHERE deleted_at IS NULL active_count, COUNT WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL deleted_count, AVG/MAX/MIN base_price for price statistics, GROUP BY category for category_distribution, GROUP BY seller for seller_distribution. Pagination wraps the filtered product list as IEcommerceMallProduct.ISummary[]. No single source table - computed from multiple JOINs and aggregations.

productCount.description:
Number of products owned by this seller matching the analytics filter criteria.

This count represents how many products the seller has created on the platform. Use this to understand product concentration across sellers.
productCount.x-autobe-specification: Computed COUNT(*) aggregation of ecommerce_mall_products.product_id grouped by seller_id. The productCount represents how many products this seller has created that match the analytics filter criteria.

seller.description:

IEcommerceMallCheckout.ISummary.IItem.description:
Validated cart item for checkout with availability status and pricing.

Represents a single item in the customer's shopping cart with validation results. Each item is checked for availability against the product variant's existence and stock quantity. The response includes computed pricing and embedded snapshots of the variant and product for display during checkout.

**Validation Status:**
- AVAILABLE: The variant exists, is not deleted, and has sufficient stock
- OUT_OF_STOCK: The variant exists but requested quantity exceeds available stock
- UNAVAILABLE: The variant has been soft-deleted and cannot be purchased

**Pricing:** Unit price is derived from the variant's price override if set, otherwise the product's base price. Subtotal is the quantity multiplied by the unit price for valid items.
IEcommerceMallCheckout.ISummary.IItem.x-autobe-specification: Computed type from ecommerce_mall_cart_items JOIN ecommerce_mall_product_variants JOIN ecommerce_mall_products. This type validates cart items for checkout availability and pricing.

code.description:
Error code categorizing the type of blocking error.

Categorizes the validation error to help clients display appropriate error indicators and take corrective actions. Error codes distinguish between product availability issues, stock problems, and configuration issues.

**Available Codes**

- PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE: Product or variant has been deleted or is no longer available for purchase
- STOCK_INSUFFICIENT: Requested quantity exceeds currently available stock
- ADDRESS_MISSING: No valid shipping address exists for this customer
- CART_EMPTY: Customer has no items in their shopping cart
code.x-autobe-specification: Enum values generated by checkout validation logic. Possible values: PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE (product/variant deleted or unavailable), STOCK_INSUFFICIENT (quantity exceeds available stock), ADDRESS_MISSING (no valid shipping address), CART_EMPTY (no items in cart).

message.description:
Human-readable error message describing the specific validation error.

Provides customers with clear, actionable information about why checkout cannot proceed. Messages are generated dynamically based on the error context and provide specific details.

**Message Examples**

- 'This product is no longer available'
- 'Only 3 items available but you requested 5'
- 'Please add a shipping address before checkout'
- 'Your cart is empty'

**Message Formatting**

Messages are localized and formatted with appropriate details such as product names, quantities, and specific requirements.

IEcommerceMallCheckout.IValidationError.description:
Checkout validation error representing blocking errors that prevent customers from proceeding to payment.

This schema defines error objects returned during checkout validation. Each error contains a code identifying the error category, a human-readable message describing the issue, and an optional reference to the specific cart item when the error relates to a particular item.

**Error Categories**

- PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE: Product or variant has been deleted or is no longer available
- STOCK_INSUFFICIENT: Requested quantity exceeds available stock
- ADDRESS_MISSING: No valid shipping address exists for checkout
- CART_EMPTY: Customer has no items in their shopping cart

Errors block checkout and must be resolved before the customer can place an order. The cartItemId field is null for errors not tied to specific cart items (ADDRESS_MISSING, CART_EMPTY).
IEcommerceMallCheckout.IValidationError.x-autobe-specification: No direct database table. Computed error object generated during checkout validation in the validateCheckout endpoint. Data sources: ecommerce_mall_cart_items (for cartItemId reference), ecommerce_mall_products, ecommerce_mall_product_variants (for availability checks), ecommerce_mall_shipping_addresses (for address validation). Code enum values from validation logic: PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE, STOCK_INSUFFICIENT, ADDRESS_MISSING, CART_EMPTY. Message is computed dynamically based on error context.

value.x-autobe-specification: Maps to ecommerce_mall_product_variant_option_values.value column. The option value such as 'Red', 'Large', or corresponding attribute value. Direct scalar mapping from the 'value' column in the normalized option values table.

IEcommerceMallCheckoutItemVariantOption.description:
Individual option key-value pair for a product variant during checkout display.

Represents a single selectable attribute such as color, size, or any product-specific option. Each option consists of a key (the attribute name) and a value (the selected option).

Use Cases:
- Displayed as variant options in cart items and checkout
- Shown during order preview and confirmation
- Used to identify specific variant combinations (e.g., Color: Red, Size: Large)
IEcommerceMallCheckoutItemVariantOption.x-autobe-specification: Computed type for checkout display. Maps key and value directly from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_option_values table columns: key maps to 'key' column, value maps to 'value' column. Each row represents one option (e.g., color=Red, size=Large). This embedded type is used within variant schemas for displaying selectable variant attributes in cart and checkout - it has no standalone identity, no id, no timestamps, and no FK reference exposed in its interface.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform - E2E Testing Requirements

## Testing Strategy

Generate comprehensive E2E test suites that cover:

### Authentication Flow Tests
1. **Customer Registration & Login**
   - Register with valid email/password → success
   - Register with existing email → duplicate error
   - Login with correct credentials → JWT token returned
   - Login with wrong password → authentication error
   - Change password with correct current password → success
   - Change password with wrong current password → error

2. **Seller Registration & Approval**
   - Register as seller → pending status
   - Login as pending seller → access to profile only
   - Admin approves seller → status becomes approved
   - Login as approved seller → full access
   - Delete account with no pending orders → success
   - Delete account with pending orders → rejection error

3. **Administrator Request Flow**
   - Any user submits admin request → pending request created
   - Super admin approves request → user becomes admin
   - Super admin promotes admin to super admin → success
   - Super admin demotes another super admin → success
   - Super admin tries to demote self → rejection

### Customer Profile Tests
1. **Profile Management**
   - Get own profile → returns display name, phone
   - Update display name → success
   - Update phone number → success

2. **Address Management**
   - Add address → address created with all fields
   - Set default address → default flag updated
   - Edit address → changes reflected
   - Delete address → removed from list
   - Get addresses → all addresses returned
   - Set another as default → switch default correctly

### Product Lifecycle Tests
1. **Product Creation**
   - Create product with all required fields → product created
   - Create product without category → validation error
   - Create product without price → validation error
   - Add multiple images → images stored with order
   - Reorder images → first image becomes main

2. **Product Variants**
   - Create variant with SKU, options, price, stock → variant created
   - Update variant price → creates snapshot
   - Delete variant with no orders → success
   - Delete variant with pending orders → rejection error

3. **Inventory Management**
   - Restock inventory → positive inventory record created
   - Adjust inventory down → negative record created
   - Get inventory history → all records returned
   - Stock reaches 0 → variant marked out of stock

4. **Product Snapshots**
   - Edit product → snapshot created
   - View own product snapshots → list returned
   - Delete product → snapshots preserved

### Shopping Flow Tests
1. **Wishlist**
   - Add product to wishlist → product in list
   - Add same product again → no duplicate
   - Remove from wishlist → removed
   - Product deleted by seller → auto-removed from wishlist

2. **Shopping Cart**
   - Add variant to cart → item added
   - Add same variant again → quantities combined
   - Update quantity → new quantity set
   - Remove item → removed from cart
   - View cart → all items with subtotals
   - Stock less than cart → warning shown

3. **Checkout Flow**
   - View checkout with valid cart → summary displayed
   - Checkout with unavailable items → error
   - Select shipping address → address saved
   - Place order (payment succeeds) → order created, stock decreased, cart cleared
   - Place order (payment fails) → no order created

### Order Management Tests
1. **Order Creation**
   - Multiple items from different sellers → multiple order items
   - Order items contain product snapshots
   - Order items contain seller profile snapshots
   - Stock decreased correctly

2. **Order Status Progression**
   - All items paid → order status "paid"
   - Any item shipped → order status "shipped"
   - All items delivered → order status "delivered"

3. **Shipping**
   - Seller creates shipment → items status changed to shipped
   - Customer views tracking → tracking info displayed
   - Customer confirms delivery → items status "delivered"
   - Auto-deliver after 14 days → items status "delivered"

4. **Cancellation Flow**
   - Customer requests cancellation → request created with reason
   - Seller approves → item cancelled, refund processed, stock restored
   - Seller rejects → item continues
   - Cannot cancel shipped item → error

5. **Refund Flow**
   - Customer requests refund (delivered, within 7 days) → request created
   - Customer requests refund (after 7 days) → error
   - Seller approves → item refunded, stock restored
   - Seller rejects → no refund

### Review System Tests
1. **Review Creation**
   - Write review for delivered item → review created
   - Write review for non-delivered item → error
   - Write duplicate review → error
   - Edit review → creates snapshot
   - Delete review → review removed, snapshot preserved

2. **Review Display**
   - Get product reviews → all reviews returned
   - Get average rating → calculated correctly
   - Deleted user review shows "deleted user"

### Seller Dashboard Tests
1. **Dashboard Summary**
   - View dashboard → correct stats
   - Total products counted
   - Pending requests counted

2. **Order Item Management**
   - List all order items → filtered by seller
   - Filter by status → correct filtering
   - View pending cancellations
   - View pending refunds

### Administrator Tests
1. **Seller Management**
   - View pending approvals → list shown
   - Approve seller → status approved
   - Reject seller → status rejected with reason
   - Suspend seller → products hidden
   - Unsuspend seller → products visible

2. **Product Oversight**
   - View all products → complete list
   - View any snapshot → access granted
   - Delete product → removed

3. **Order Oversight**
   - View all orders → complete list
   - Force-cancel item → cancelled, refund, stock restored
   - Force-refund item → refunded, stock restored

4. **User Management**
   - Ban customer → cannot login
   - Unban customer → can login again
   - Ban seller → cannot login, existing orders preserved

## Test Data Setup
- Create test users for each role (customer, seller, admin, super_admin)
- Create test categories with subcategories
- Create test products with variants and images
- Create test inventory records

## Test Cleanup
- Each test cleans up its own data
- Use transactions to rollback after each test
- Reset inventory to known state

## Edge Cases to Test
1. Concurrent cart updates (same variant added by multiple users)
2. Stock race conditions during checkout
3. Price changes between cart and checkout (snapshot preserves old price)
4. Seller deleted while customer has items in cart
5. Product deleted while in someone's wishlist
6. Cancellation after partial shipment
7. Refund request exactly at 7-day boundary

Test that a guest visitor can create a new session by providing a valid device fingerprint.

scenario.draft:
Test the guest upsert endpoint for updating an existing guest record with partial browsing context update.

**Prerequisites:** Authenticate as admin using POST /ecommerceMall/auth/admin/join to obtain valid admin JWT tokens.

**Test Steps:**
1. Call PATCH /ecommerceMall/admin/guests with a unique fingerprint and complete context (ipAddress='192.168.1.100', userAgent='Mozilla/5.0') to create initial guest record
2. Record the returned guest id and all timestamps from the response
3. Wait 1 second to ensure timestamp difference
4. Call PATCH /ecommerceMall/admin/guests with the SAME fingerprint but ONLY ipAddress='10.0.0.50' (omit userAgent field)
5. Validate the response contains:
   - Same UUID identifier (id field unchanged - record was updated, not recreated)
   - Updated ipAddress reflecting the new value '10.0.0.50'
   - userAgent retained from step 2 (not cleared when omitted in update)
   - lastActiveAt updated to a more recent timestamp than step 2
   - createdAt remaining unchanged from step 2 (preserves original creation time)
   - updatedAt updated to current timestamp
6. Call PATCH /ecommerceMall/admin/guests with the SAME fingerprint but ONLY userAgent='Chrome/120.0' (omit ipAddress)
7. Validate the response contains:
   - Same UUID identifier (id unchanged)
   - ipAddress retained from step 4 (not cleared when omitted)
   - userAgent updated to 'Chrome/120.0'
   - lastActiveAt updated again

**Business Logic Validation:**
- Existing guest record is updated in-place when fingerprint matches an existing record
- lastActiveAt is refreshed on every upsert call for session continuity tracking
- Optional fields can be omitted without affecting other stored values (partial updates)
- Record identity is preserved via fingerprint matching
- createdAt timestamp is immutable after creation (never reset on updates)
- Multiple updates to same fingerprint maintain single guest record

scenario.draft:
Test retrieving an existing admin audit log entry by its unique identifier. This validates the primary success path for the audit log retrieval endpoint.

**Pre-conditions:**
1. An administrator account exists in the system (created via admin join)
2. An administrative action has been performed that generated an audit log entry (e.g., approving a seller)

- Response body contains complete audit log record with all required fields:
  - id: UUID of the audit log entry
  - admin: Nested admin summary object with id, email, and name of the administrator who performed the action
  - action: String describing the type of action (e.g., 'approve_seller', 'suspend_seller', 'delete_product')
  - resourceType: Type of resource affected (e.g., 'seller', 'product', 'customer')
  - resourceId: UUID of the affected resource
  - details: Additional context (may be null or contain JSON with reason/rejection text)
  - ipAddress: IP address from which the admin performed the action
  - userAgent: User agent string of the admin's browser/client (may be null)
  - createdAt: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the action occurred
- Admin information correctly joined from ecommerce_mall_admins table
- All fields match the expected data types per IEcommerceMallAdminAuditLog schema

scenario.draft:
Test customer isolation when retrieving cart items.

**Setup**: Register two different customers. Customer A adds an item to cart. Customer B attempts to retrieve Customer A's cart item.

**Steps**:
1. Call POST /ecommerceMall/auth/customer/join to register Customer A
2. Call POST /ecommerceMall/customer/me/cart/items to add item to Customer A's cart
3. Extract cartItemId from Customer A's cart item
4. Call POST /ecommerceMall/auth/customer/join to register Customer B (different account)
5. Call GET /ecommerceMall/customer/me/cart/items/{cartItemId} using Customer A's cartItemId but authenticated as Customer B

**Expected Results**:
- HTTP 404 Not Found status
- Customer B cannot access Customer A's cart items

**Business Rules Validated**:
- Cart Customer Isolation (ID: 469): Each customer has exactly one shopping cart. A customer cannot access, view, or modify another customer's cart under any circumstances. The system enforces strict customer isolation for all cart operations.

**Pre-conditions**:
- Customer is authenticated with valid session token
- A product variant has been soft-deleted by the seller (deleted_at is not null)

**Test Steps**:
1. Authenticate as a customer using POST /ecommerceMall/auth/customer/join with valid email and password
2. Attempt to add a deleted variant by calling POST /ecommerceMall/customer/me/cart/items with productVariantId of the deleted variant

**Expected Results**:
- HTTP 404 response indicating variant not found
- Error message indicates the variant does not exist or is unavailable
- No cart item is created
- This validates that deleted variants cannot be added to cart (per business rule: 'Deleted variants cannot be included in checkout under any circumstances')

- Response body contains the updated cart item
- quantity field equals 5
- subtotal is correctly computed (quantity * variant price)

scenario.draft:
Test that updating a cart item fails with 404 when the associated product variant has been deleted by the seller. This validates the business rule that deleted variants become unavailable in the cart.

**Steps:**
1. Register a new customer account via POST /auth/customer/join
2. Add a product variant to the customer's cart via POST /customer/me/cart with {variantId, quantity: 1}
3. Record the cartItemId from the response
4. Seller deletes the product variant (via seller operation - variant deletion)
5. Customer attempts to update the cart item quantity via PUT /customer/me/cart/items/{cartItemId} with {quantity: 2}

**Validations:**
- Response status is 404 Not Found
- Error message indicates the cart item is unavailable
- Response does not reveal whether the item exists (security through obscurity)
- Customer can still view their cart showing the unavailable item

scenario.draft:
Test scenario for a seller successfully viewing their own product snapshot.

Prerequisites:
1. Authenticate as a seller using POST /auth/seller/join with valid email and password to obtain JWT token
2. Verify the seller has approval_status = 'approved' before proceeding
3. Create a category using POST /ecommerceMall/admin/admin/categories (required prerequisite for product creation)
4. Create a product using POST /ecommerceMall/seller/sellers/me/products with name, description, basePrice, and categoryId to trigger automatic snapshot creation
5. List product snapshots using GET /ecommerceMall/seller/sellers/me/products/{productId}/snapshots to obtain a valid snapshotId

Test Execution:
1. Call GET /ecommerceMall/seller/sellers/me/products/{productId}/snapshots/{snapshotId} with valid productId and snapshotId
2. Verify response status is 200 OK
3. Validate response body contains IEcommerceMallProductSnapshot.IInvert structure with all required fields:
   - id: UUID of the snapshot
   - name: Product name as it appeared at snapshot creation
   - description: Product description at snapshot time
   - basePrice: Base price at snapshot creation
   - categoryName: Category name preserved at snapshot time
   - createdAt: ISO 8601 timestamp when snapshot was created
   - product: Parent product summary (IEcommerceMallProduct.ISummary)
   - productSnapshotImages: Array of images with id, url, displayOrder, createdAt, updatedAt
   - productSnapshotVariants: Array of variants with id, price, quantity, skuCode, optionValues (each with id, key, value)
4. Verify variants are ordered by created_at ascending
5. Verify images are ordered by display_order ascending
6. Validate optionValues array is nested within each variant

This test validates the primary success path for sellers accessing their product modification history for dispute resolution purposes.

scenario.draft:
Test that a seller can successfully add inventory (restock) to a product variant with a positive quantity change.

**Precondition**: Seller must be authenticated and approved. A product with a variant must exist and be owned by the seller.

**Test Steps**:
1. Authenticate as seller (POST /auth/seller/join)
2. Create a product (POST /sellers/me/products) with required fields: name, description, basePrice, categoryId
3. Create a product variant (POST /sellers/me/products/{productId}/variants) with skuCode and optionValues
4. Verify initial stock is 0 (new variants start with zero stock per business rules in section 602)
5. Call PATCH /seller/variants/{variantId}/inventory with quantityChange: 100, reason: 'restock'
6. Verify response returns inventory record with quantityChange: 100, reason: 'restock', UUID and timestamp
7. Verify variant's current stock is now 100
8. Call GET /seller/sellers/me/variants/{variantId}/inventory to verify history shows the restock record

**Expected Results**:
- HTTP 200 OK with created inventory record
- Record contains positive quantityChange (100)
- Reason matches 'restock'
- Current stock calculated correctly via sum of all inventory records
- Inventory history displays records in descending timestamp order

scenario.draft:
Test that a seller can successfully subtract inventory (adjustment) from a product variant when stock is available.

**Precondition**: Seller must be authenticated and approved. A product with a variant must exist with current stock > 0.

**Test Steps**:
1. Authenticate as seller
2. Create a product
3. Create a product variant
4. First, add initial inventory via PATCH /seller/variants/{variantId}/inventory with quantityChange: 50, reason: 'restock' to establish stock
5. Verify current stock is 50 after restock
6. Then, perform the adjustment operation: Call PATCH /seller/variants/{variantId}/inventory with quantityChange: 5, reason: 'damaged'
7. Verify response returns inventory record with quantityChange: -5 (negative for subtraction), reason: 'damaged'
8. Verify variant's current stock is now 45 (50 - 5)
9. Call GET /seller/sellers/me/variants/{variantId}/inventory to verify inventory history shows both records in descending timestamp order

**Expected Results**:
- HTTP 200 OK with created inventory record for adjustment
- quantityChange is stored as negative value (-5) for adjustments
- Reason matches 'damaged'
- Current stock reflects subtraction: 50 - 5 = 45
- Both restock and adjustment records appear in inventory history

scenario.draft:
Test that the system correctly rejects an inventory adjustment when the requested subtraction quantity exceeds the current available stock.

**Precondition**: Seller must be authenticated and approved. A product with a variant must exist with limited stock.

**Test Steps**:
1. Authenticate as seller
2. Create a product
3. Create a product variant
4. First, add limited inventory via PATCH /seller/variants/{variantId}/inventory with quantityChange: 10, reason: 'restock' to establish stock
5. Verify current stock is 10 after restock
6. Then, attempt to subtract more than available: Call PATCH /seller/variants/{variantId}/inventory with quantityChange: 15, reason: 'correction'
7. Verify HTTP 400 Bad Request response
8. Verify error message indicates adjustment exceeds available stock
9. Verify original stock of 10 remains unchanged (no partial deduction)
10. Verify no additional inventory record was created for the failed adjustment by checking inventory history

**Expected Results**:
- HTTP 400 Bad Request
- Error message clarifies the quantity exceeds current stock
- No inventory record created for the failed adjustment
- Current stock remains at 10 (unchanged)

**Business Rule Validated**: The system shall reject an adjustment operation if the requested quantity exceeds the current available stock (per section 316 Inventory Record Creation and Tracking)

- Item shows correct product name from the added variant

- Item quantity matches the quantity added (default 1)
- Item subtotal equals quantity multiplied by variant price (or product base price if variant price is null)
- Cart total equals the single item subtotal
- Response includes cart timestamps (createdAt, updatedAt)
- Cart isolation is enforced - only this customer's items are visible

- Response should include timestamps (createdAt, updatedAt)
- sellerResponseAt should be null (not yet responded)
- snapshots array should be empty initially

**Business Logic Verified**:
- Item is in 'delivered' status
- Refund window is within 7 days of delivery
- Only this specific item is affected, not other items in order

scenario.draft:
Test that when a single order contains items from multiple sellers, each seller can only view and retrieve their own order items, not items from other sellers.

**Pre-conditions**:
- Multiple approved sellers with products
- One customer who purchases from both sellers in a single order

1. Authenticate as Seller A and create a product
2. Authenticate as Seller B and create a different product
3. Authenticate as a customer and add both products to cart
4. Checkout to create a single order containing items from both sellers
5. As Seller A, call GET /seller/sellers/me/orders/items
6. As Seller B, call GET /seller/sellers/me/orders/items

**Expected Results**:
- Both calls return successfully with 200 status
- Seller A's response contains ONLY order items where product belongs to Seller A
- Seller B's response contains ONLY order items where product belongs to Seller B
- Seller A does NOT see Seller B's items even though they are in the same order
- Seller B does NOT see Seller A's items
- Each order item in the response includes:
  - Product snapshot frozen at purchase time (preserves what customer saw when ordering)
  - Seller profile snapshot frozen at purchase time
  - Correct parent order reference showing the same order_number for both sellers
- This validates the multi-seller order isolation where order items are filtered by seller's product ownership

scenario.draft:
Test that a seller can successfully retrieve shipment details for a shipment they created.

Precondition: A seller must have created a shipment containing one or more order items with paid status.

Steps:
1. Register and authenticate as a seller with approved status
2. Register as a customer and create a shipping address
3. Create an order with items from the seller's products
4. Create a shipment with the order items, specifying carrier name and tracking number
5. Call GET /seller/shipments/{shipmentId} with the created shipment ID

Expected Results:
- Response returns HTTP 200 with complete shipment details
- Response includes shipment ID, carrier name, tracking number, createdAt timestamp
- Response includes the parent order reference with order number
- Response includes seller information
- Response includes all shipment items with order item details (quantity, unitPrice, status)
- Each shipment item includes frozen product snapshot with name, description, basePrice, categoryName
- Each shipment item includes variant options showing selected options (e.g., color, size)
- Each shipment item includes frozen seller profile snapshot with shopName

functions.name: test_api_shipment_creation_with_multiple_items

scenario.draft:
Test that creating a shipment with order items from different sellers is rejected.

**Pre-conditions**:
1. Register and approve two different sellers (Seller A and Seller B)
2. Customer places order containing items from both Seller A and Seller B
3. Order contains items with 'paid' status from multiple sellers

**Test Steps**:
1. Authenticate as Seller A
2. Attempt to send POST request to /seller/shipments with:
   - orderId: the order ID containing mixed seller items
   - carrier: "DHL"
   - trackingNumber: "DHL987654321"
   - itemIds: array containing orderItemIds from BOTH Seller A and Seller B

**Validation Points**:
- Response status 400 Bad Request
- Error message indicates that all items must belong to the same seller
- No shipment record is created
- Order items retain their 'paid' status unchanged
- System enforces single-seller-per-shipment business rule

- Snapshots ordered by createdAt descending (newest first)
- Pagination metadata present (current page, total pages, records count)
- Snapshot should reflect state at moment of seller approval

   - userAgent: client user agent string (nullable)
   - createdAt: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the action occurred
4. Verify the admin object in response matches the authenticated admin who performed the action
5. Verify all fields are present and properly typed according to IEcommerceMallAdminAuditLog schema

scenario.draft:
Test stock validation with sufficient stock - all items available for checkout.

**Scenario**: Customer has cart items where the quantity in cart does not exceed available stock. The endpoint should return validation results showing all items are available without warnings.

**Setup**:
1. Register admin account via POST /auth/admin/join
2. Register seller account via POST /auth/seller/join
3. Admin approves seller via POST /admin/admin/sellers/{sellerId}/approve
4. Seller creates product via POST /seller/sellers/me/products
5. Seller creates product variant via POST /seller/sellers/me/products/{productId}/variants
6. Seller adds inventory stock (10 units) via POST /seller/sellers/me/variants/{variantId}/inventory
7. Register customer account via POST /auth/customer/join
8. Customer adds variant to cart (quantity 5) via POST /customer/customers/me/cart

**Execution**:
- Call PATCH /customer/customers/me/cart/stock with empty cartItemIds array to validate all cart items

**Expected Results**:
- Response returns cart item validation with:
  - cartItemId: matches the added cart item UUID
  - variantId: matches the variant UUID
  - skuCode: correct SKU code from variant
  - cartQuantity: 5 (requested quantity in cart)
  - availableStock: 10 (current stock)
  - hasWarning: false (cart quantity does not exceed available stock)
  - isAvailable: true (stock > 0, item can be fulfilled)
  - warningMessage: null (no warning for available items)

**Validation Points**:
- hasWarning should be false when cartQuantity <= availableStock
- isAvailable should be true when availableStock > 0
- warningMessage should be null for items without warnings
- All items pass stock validation for checkout

Test stock validation with stock warning when cart quantity exceeds available stock but stock is not zero.

**Scenario**: Customer has a cart item where the requested quantity exceeds available stock but stock is not zero. The endpoint should return a warning flag indicating stock shortage while still marking the item as available.

  - cartItemId: matches the added cart item UUID
  - variantId: matches the variant UUID
  - skuCode: correct SKU code from variant
  - cartQuantity: 10 (requested quantity in cart)

- warningMessage should contain the requested and available quantities

- Response should return HTTP 200
- Response should contain pagination metadata (current, limit, records, pages)
- Data array should contain at least one snapshot
- Each snapshot should include: id (UUID), cancellationRequestId, reason (from original request), status ('approved'), createdAt
- Snapshots should be ordered by createdAt descending (most recent first)
- cancellationRequestId should match the requestId parameter

instruction:
# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform - Implementation Requirements

## Implementation Scope

Implement all service providers and business logic for the complete e-commerce platform based on the previously generated database schema, API interfaces, and tests.

## Core Modules to Implement

### 1. Authentication Services
- Customer registration, login, password change, account deletion
- Seller registration, login, password change, account deletion (with validation)
- Admin registration request, approval workflow
- JWT token generation and validation
- Role-based access control middleware

### 2. Customer Services
- Profile management (display name, phone)
- Address CRUD with default address functionality
- Wishlist management
- Shopping cart operations

### 3. Seller Services
- Seller profile with snapshot creation on edit
- Product CRUD with snapshot creation
- Product image upload and reordering
- Product variant management with snapshot creation
- Inventory management (restock, adjust, history)
- Order item processing (view, ship)
- Cancellation request handling (approve/reject)
- Refund request handling (approve/reject)
- Dashboard statistics

### 4. Product Services
- Public product search with filters (category, price, stock, sort)
- Product listing with pagination
- Product detail with variants, images, reviews
- Category browsing

### 5. Order Services
- Checkout process with address selection
- Payment integration (mock implementation)
- Order creation with:
  - Stock deduction
  - Cart clearing
  - Product snapshot creation
  - Seller profile snapshot creation
- Order history with pagination
- Shipment management
- Delivery confirmation (manual and auto after 14 days)

### 6. Cancellation & Refund Services
- Cancellation request creation and validation
- Cancellation approval with stock restoration
- Refund request creation (7-day validation)
- Refund approval with stock restoration
- Snapshot creation for all status changes

### 7. Review Services
- Review creation (delivered item validation)
- Review editing with snapshot
- Review deletion (preserves snapshot)
- Rating calculation

### 8. Administrator Services
- Seller approval/rejection with reason
- Seller suspension/unsuspension
- Category management
- Product oversight
- Order force-cancel/force-refund
- Customer ban/unban
- Seller ban/unban
- Admin promotion/demotion

## Business Rules to Implement

1. **Snapshot System**: Every edit to products, variants, seller profiles, reviews creates immutable snapshot
2. **Soft Delete**: Customers deleted → profile removed, orders/reviews preserved; Sellers deleted → products removed, orders preserved
3. **Stock Management**: Real-time stock calculation from inventory history
4. **Order Item Status**: Individual status per item, derived order status
5. **Deletion Guards**: Cannot delete variants/products with pending orders
6. **7-Day Refund Window**: Only within 7 days of delivery
7. **Seller Suspension**: Hides products but allows order processing
8. **Auto-Delivery**: 14 days after shipping

## Technical Requirements

- Use TypeScript with strict typing
- NestJS service architecture
- Prisma ORM for database operations
- Input validation with class-validator
- Error handling with appropriate HTTP status codes
- Transaction support for multi-table operations
- Pagination for all list endpoints

plan.thinking: IEcommerceMallProductVariant.ICreate is a Create DTO type that maps directly to the ecommerce_mall_product_variants database table. This is a collectable DTO because it is used for inserting new product variant records. The Create DTO contains skuCode and price fields that map to database columns, and optionValues creates related records in ecommerce_mall_product_variant_option_values as part of atomic composition. References needed: productId from path parameter links to ecommerce_mall_products, seller and session from auth context.

IEcommerceMallWishlistItem.ICreate is a Create DTO that inserts wishlist items into ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items table. Maps directly to database. Collectable. productId comes from request body. wishlist_id is auto-determined from authenticated customer's session (one-to-one relationship). References from auth context: customer (authorized actor) and customer session.

IEcommerceMallCancellationRequest.ICreate is a Create DTO for cancellation requests. Maps to ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests table (confirmed via x-autobe-database-schema). Contains only 'reason' field. The order_item_id comes from path parameter itemId, customer_id from JWT session, and seller_id is derived from the order item. Collectable with external references.

IEcommerceMallRefundRequest.ICreate is a Create DTO for customer refund requests on delivered order items. Maps to ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table with reason field from request body. External references: order item ID from path parameter {itemId} (ecommerce_mall_order_items) and customer ID from authenticated JWT (ecommerce_mall_customers). Seller ID is derived from order item's product relationship, not a direct reference. Collectable DTO.

IEcommerceMallShipment.ICreate is a Create DTO for shipment creation. Maps to ecommerce_mall_shipments table with carrier and tracking_number fields. The authenticated seller comes from JWT token (authorized actor), and order/order items are derived from the itemId path parameter. This is a collectable DTO as it creates new database records.

IEcommerceMallOrder.ICreate is a Create DTO for order creation. Maps to ecommerce_mall_orders table via x-autobe-database-schema annotation. Customer ID is extracted from authenticated JWT token (authorized actor), shippingAddressId is provided in request body. Collectable DTO.

IEcommerceMallShippingAddress.ICreate is a Create DTO used in POST /ecommerceMall/customer/customers/me/addresses. Maps directly to ecommerce_mall_shipping_addresses table with all address fields in the DTO body. Customer ID is resolved from authenticated session (JWT), so references needed for customer and session entities from auth context.

IEcommerceMallCartItem.ICreate is a Create DTO that inserts cart items into the ecommerce_mall_cart_items table. The DTO contains productVariantId and quantity in the body. The cart FK (ecommerce_mall_cart_id) is derived from the authenticated customer session and auto-created if needed - this is an external reference from authorized session. The customer FK also comes from the authorized actor context. Both references are needed for the collector function.

IEcommerceMallCategory.ICreate is a Create DTO for category creation. Maps directly to ecommerce_mall_categories table. Contains name (required), description (optional), and parent_id (optional FK for subcategory). All FKs are in the DTO body itself - no external references from path parameters or auth context needed. Collectable DTO.

IEcommerceMallProduct.ICreate is a Create DTO for product creation via POST /ecommerceMall/seller/sellers/me/products. Maps directly to ecommerce_mall_products table with seller reference from authorized actor session. Collectable.
IEcommerceMallProductImage.ICreate is a Create DTO for uploading product images. Maps to ecommerce_mall_product_images table with productId from path parameter and seller from authorized actor.

IEcommerceMallProductVariantOptionValue.ICreate is a Create DTO that maps directly to the ecommerce_mall_product_variant_option_values database table (confirmed via x-autobe-database-schema annotation). The product_variant_id is provided via path parameter variantId. The seller is authenticated via JWT token and must own the product to create option values.

IEcommerceMallInventoryRecord.ICreate is a Create DTO used for inventory record creation. It maps directly to the ecommerce_mall_inventory_records database table with quantityChange (maps to quantity_change) and reason fields. The variantId FK comes from the path parameter, not the DTO body. This is collectable.

IEcommerceMallCart.ICreate is a Create DTO for adding items to customer cart. Maps to ecommerce_mall_cart_items table based on specification. variantId is in request body, customer_id is from JWT (from authorized actor). Collectable with references from auth context.

IEcommerceMallReview.ICreate is a Create DTO that maps to ecommerce_mall_reviews table. Customer ID comes from authorized actor (JWT), product_id comes from the order item (via path parameter itemId), and order_item_id comes from path parameter {itemId}. This is a collectable Create DTO.

IEcommerceMallSellerSuspension.ICreate is a Create DTO for suspending sellers. Maps to ecommerce_mall_seller_suspensions table. Collectable with seller ID from path parameter and admin ID from authorized actor.

IEcommerceMallSellerAdminRequest.ICreate is a Create DTO for submitting seller admin privilege requests. Maps to ecommerce_mall_seller_admin_requests table with seller reference from authenticated session.

IEcommerceMallSeller.ICreate is a Create DTO for seller registration/reregistration. Maps to ecommerce_mall_sellers table via x-autobe-database-schema annotation. Email and password fields are stored directly to sellers table. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) stored in ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions. No external FK references from path parameters or auth context. Collectable.

Collectable Create DTO for admin promotion audit records. Maps to ecommerce_mall_admin_promotions table. Admin being promoted comes from path parameter userId, super admin performing action comes from authorized actor session.

IEcommerceMallOrderItem is a Read DTO used for order item API responses. It has x-autobe-database-schema: ecommerce_mall_order_items with direct column mappings (id, created_at, quantity, unit_price, status) and JOIN relations to related tables (order, productSnapshot, sellerProfileSnapshot, productVariant, product). Transformable to ecommerce_mall_order_items.

IEcommerceMallSeller is a read DTO mapping to ecommerce_mall_sellers table. The x-autobe-database-schema annotation explicitly indicates ecommerce_mall_sellers. Direct fields: id, email, approval_status, rejection_reason, rejected_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. JOIN relations: profile (one-to-one to seller_profiles), sellerApprovals (one-to-many), sellerSuspensions (one-to-many). Excludes password_hash for security. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallShipmentItem.IInvert is a read DTO with x-autobe-database-schema: ecommerce_mall_shipment_items. Direct mapping to junction table. Contains shipment item id, created_at, and parent context via joins to orderItem, productSnapshot, productSnapshotVariant, and shipment. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallAdminRequest.ISummary is a read DTO for paginated admin request listings. Maps to ecommerce_mall_admin_requests table with LEFT JOIN for reviewer (ecommerce_mall_super_admins) and conditional JOIN for polymorphic actor (customer/seller). Transformable.

IEcommerceMallCartItem is a read DTO for shopping cart items. The x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirms it maps directly to ecommerce_mall_cart_items table. Contains direct column mappings (id, quantity, created_at, updated_at), belongs-to relation to productVariant, computed subtotal field. Product obtained via JOIN through variant. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallCategory is a read DTO for API responses. The schema shows x-autobe-database-schema: ecommerce_mall_categories with direct field mappings (id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and JOINs for parent relation and HAS-MANY for subcategories. This is database-backed and directly maps to the ecommerce_mall_categories table.

IEcommerceMallCustomer.IInvert is a read DTO for authenticated customer profile viewing. The schema has x-autobe-database-schema: ecommerce_mall_customers with direct column mappings for id, email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Nested relations (profile, shippingAddresses, cart, wishlist) are join-based but the root entity maps directly to ecommerce_mall_customers. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallCustomer is a complete customer entity for API responses. The schema explicitly has x-autobe-database-schema: ecommerce_mall_customers. It is a Read DTO used for API responses, DB-backed, and has direct mapping to the database table. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallOrder is a Read DTO used for API order responses. Maps to ecommerce_mall_orders table with direct column mappings: id, order_number, subtotal, shipping_cost, total_amount, status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Nested relations (customer, shippingAddress, orderItems, shipments) are joins/compositions. This is transformable - databaseSchemaName is ecommerce_mall_orders.

IEcommerceMallProduct is a transformable Read DTO. The interface schema explicitly shows x-autobe-database-schema: "ecommerce_mall_products", confirming it maps to the ecommerce_mall_products database table. This is a complete product entity used for API responses, containing computed fields (inStock, priceRange, ratingAverage, ratingCount) and nested relations (seller, category, images, variants), but the primary table mapping is ecommerce_mall_products.

IEcommerceMallAdminRequest is a read DTO for administrator privilege requests. Has x-autobe-database-schema: 'ecommerce_mall_admin_requests' annotation confirming direct table mapping. Maps to ecommerce_mall_admin_requests table with fields id, actor_type, requested_grade, reason, status, reviewed_reason, timestamps and relations (reviewer, customer, seller). Transformable.

IEcommerceMallReview.ISummary is a Read DTO for listing reviews with database mapping to ecommerce_mall_reviews table. It has direct field mappings (id, rating, content, createdAt) and BELONGS-TO relations to customer and product. This is a transformable DTO.

IEcommerceMallAdmin.ISummary is a read DTO for admin list displays. It maps directly to ecommerce_mall_admins table with id, email, name, created_at, and optional deleted_at fields. All properties are direct column mappings with no joins or computed fields. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallCustomer.ISummary is a read DTO for customer list displays. It maps directly to ecommerce_mall_customers table with a JOIN to ecommerce_mall_customer_profiles for the nested profile object. The DTO contains fields from both tables (customer fields + profile fields) and a computed status field. This is a transformable DTO as it represents database-backed entity data for API responses.

IEcommerceMallCustomerProfile is a read DTO returned by GET /customers/me and PATCH /customers/me endpoints. It maps directly to the ecommerce_mall_customer_profiles database table with id, display_name, phone, created_at, updated_at fields, plus a nested customer object via belongs-to relation. This is a database-backed entity with direct table mapping.

IEcommerceMallSuperAdmin.ISummary is a summary DTO for paginated list displays of super administrator accounts. The interface schema x-autobe-database-schema confirms direct mapping to ecommerce_mall_super_admins table. Properties include id, email, createdAt, updatedAt, and computed isDeleted. This is a read DTO used for API list responses, not request parameters. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallCustomerSession is a read DTO that maps directly to the ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions database table. The interface schema confirms x-autobe-database-schema: ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions with direct field mappings (id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, updated_at, expired_at) and a BELONGS-TO relation to ecommerce_mall_customers.
